AVPT is a low-attention, mid-cap discovery candidate in SaaS data governance, resilience, and agentic AI governance, especially around Microsoft/Google cloud ecosystems.
FROG is an indirect AI infrastructure software candidate: AI coding agents and model deployment may increase need for artifact, model, package, and MCP governance.
The node’s strongest public-company mappings are identity governance, data security posture management, AI-agent governance, and secure software/AI supply-chain systems of record.

Layer 2 should verify financial materiality: ARR contribution, module attach rates, customer case studies, marketplace traction, and whether AI-specific products are paid SKUs rather than marketing overlays.
SAIL should be tracked as the reference public identity-governance name for AI-agent and machine-identity security, with survival dependent on evidence of module monetization and net-retention lift.
TENB is a mid-cap cloud/AI exposure-management candidate; verify whether AI/cloud security claims translate into ARR mix and enterprise expansion.
AVPT is an underfollowed SaaS data-governance and resilience candidate tied to Microsoft/Agent 365 and enterprise AI data readiness; evidence must confirm paid adoption beyond marketing.

PD is a speculative small-cap automation and incident-response control-plane candidate for AI operations complexity; needs proof of growth reacceleration, usage-based revenue contribution, and FedRAMP/public-sector traction.
The strongest software chokepoint signals in this node are non-human identity governance, AI/cloud exposure management, SaaS data governance, and autonomous incident/workflow automation.

Do not advance AI-branded infrastructure software names unless future layers verify ARR, retention, module attach, marketplace traction, regulated-customer adoption, or explicit AI-agent/data-governance use cases.
SAIL is a high-priority underfollowed identity-governance candidate for AI-agent entitlement, machine identity, and enterprise access governance verification.
TENB is a high-priority underfollowed AI/cloud exposure-management candidate because it has explicit AI-SPM, DSPM, AI Exposure, and Tenable One evidence.
PD is a speculative small-cap automation and AIOps candidate; survival into later layers requires proof that AI/agentic operations capabilities affect ARR expansion or retention.

For this node, the strongest chokepoint framing is not generic AI software but governance/control-plane software: identity entitlements, machine identities, AI posture management, cloud exposure, observability, and incident automation.

VRNS should be added to the next data-security/DSPM-specific pass; it appears relevant to sensitive-data exposure and generative-AI risk but was excluded here to keep the candidate list capped at four.
SAIL should remain the reference identity-governance anchor for this node, especially for AI-agent and machine-identity governance, but must be tested for product-level ARR contribution.
VRNS is a strong underfollowed candidate for AI data-security posture and AI TRiSM convergence; key survival evidence is SaaS ARR acceleration and AllTrue.ai integration traction.
AVPT is an underappreciated AI-readiness and agent-governance beneficiary within SaaS data protection, particularly around Microsoft 365/Copilot and multi-SaaS governance.
PD is a speculative but relevant small-cap operations-control-plane candidate; verify whether AI agents and AIOps features can change ARR growth trajectory.

Next pass should compare these names against higher-attention platforms such as Okta, ServiceNow, Datadog, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Microsoft to isolate where underfollowed exposure is genuinely differentiated versus already priced into broad platform narratives.

The list intentionally keeps one identity-governance reference name and three smaller or more niche underfollowed discovery candidates. Inclusion is research-prioritization only, not a buy/sell view. Expanded the universe toward US-listed software control-plane vendors that may benefit from AI workload sprawl: identity governance for non-human and AI-agent identities, cloud/AI exposure management, data governance for AI readiness, and incident/workflow automation. The pass intentionally avoids GPU/hyperscaler megacaps and treats AI claims as evidence-gated unless tied to concrete product modules, marketplaces, regulated customers, or recurring enterprise adoption. Layer 1B expansion found a small set of US-listed software names with plausible second-order exposure to AI workload sprawl through identity governance, AI/cloud exposure management, observability, and incident/workflow automation.
